name: Superconducting magnetic energy store
effect: very cold metals lose all electrical resistance
how: A large coil of superconducting wire is kept frozen in an insulated cryostat. Because the wire has no resistance, a current fed into it keeps circling forever, storing energy in its magnetic field. It can be released in a split second to steady a power grid.
why: Electricity that circles a loop forever until needed.
real: Superconducting magnetic energy storage, pilot units 1980s-90s
